# ADR-0014: UUID v7 primary keys generated by a database function

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-30
- Resolves: spec gap C4 (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 requires UUID v7; Postgres 16 has no
  built-in generator, `uuidv7()` arrives in Postgres 18)

## Decision

- The baseline migration defines `uuid_generate_v7()` (plpgsql, RFC 9562: 48-bit Unix
  milliseconds, version 7, variant `10`, 74 random bits from `pgcrypto.gen_random_bytes`).
- Tables use `DEFAULT uuid_generate_v7()`, so IDs are correct even for rows inserted by raw
  SQL, imports or migrations, not only through the ORM.
- When the platform moves to Postgres 18, the function can become a thin wrapper around the
  built-in `uuidv7()` with no schema change.

## Verification

`packages/db/src/baseline.int.test.ts`: version and variant bits, embedded timestamp within
the test's time window, uniqueness across 1,000 IDs, and millisecond ordering.

## Consequences

- Time-ordered keys keep B-tree inserts local and make IDs roughly sortable by creation time.
- IDs leak creation time to anyone who sees them. That is acceptable: every endpoint is
  authenticated and tenant-scoped, and IDs are not used as secrets.
